facts.label: Financial base view
facts.text: The consolidated Group moved from no borrowings (September 30, 2025) to $4,992 million of borrowings after the December 2025 Merus financing, so the reported base now has two regimes: a pre-acquisition year with net cash and a post-acquisition year with net debt. Debt is carried at amortized cost in four instruments (Term A Loans, Term B Loans, Secured Notes, Unsecured Notes), all disclosed with current and non-current carrying values, and the Group had $1,860 million of cash and no marketable securities at September 30, 2026. On a carrying-value basis net debt was $3,132 million, down from $3,559 million at December 31, 2025, with principal repayments of $288 million in nine months 2026. The income base is royalty-led (royalties $2,699 million of $3,238 million revenue) and operating profit is $986 million for the nine months, with adjusted operating profit of $1,108 million on the company's own non-IFRS definition. The issuer reports no EBITDA, and the depreciation and amortization needed for a last-twelve-months EBITDA is not supplied for FY2025, so the leverage chart cannot be populated; EBIT-based reference ratios are given instead and are labelled as such. Interest cover is calculable for Q1 2026 and nine months 2026 only. Undrawn committed facilities, covenant levels and contractual maturities are Not supplied. The base is therefore sufficient for reported-fact extraction, cash and net debt, cash conversion and interest cover on a nine-month basis, and restricted for LTM leverage, liquidity headroom, maturity profile and covenant analysis.

facts.label: Acquisition leverage rests on one intangible asset
facts.text: Evidence: borrowings of 4,992 against shareholders' equity of 6,333, and goodwill and intangibles of 9,197 including acquired IPR&D of 8,237, which is 63.7% of total assets of 12,936 (Q3 2026 report page:5, page:34, page:40). Risk mechanic: the Merus purchase was accounted for as an asset acquisition concentrated in a single identifiable asset, petosemtamab (Q3 2026 report page:39), so the balance-sheet value that backs the debt depends on one pipeline asset that is not yet generating revenue; an adverse trial or regulatory outcome would impair the IPR&D and equity but would not by itself change cash debt service. Credit implication: asset-based recovery cover is weak relative to debt, and creditor protection rests on royalty cash flows and the covenants, not on the asset base. October 2026 topline results for petosemtamab were reported as meeting both primary endpoints (Q3 2026 report page:4); that is a post-quarter event and a management announcement, with no financial effect quantified in the supplied sources.

facts.label: Margin compression reflects launch investment and is guided to continue
facts.text: Evidence: adjusted operating expenses of 1,896 versus 1,489 (up 27%) against revenue up 22%, giving operating margin of 30.4% versus 37.8% (Q3 2026 report page:2, page:5). The full-year guidance of adjusted operating profit of 1,065 to 1,385 and revenue of 4,325 to 4,525 implies a fourth quarter below the third: adjusted operating profit of minus 43 to 277 (midpoint 117) versus 452 in Q3 2026, because 9M adjusted operating profit is 1,108. Risk mechanic: spending ahead of launches in 2027 is front-loaded while royalty growth is tied to partners' sales. Credit implication: EBITDA available for interest is not going to grow in line with revenue in the near term; the interest cover ratios above should be read as strong-quarter outcomes, not as a floor. Management language: guidance assumes no significant new agreements (page:6).

facts.label: Cash flow covers debt service, but quality is mixed
facts.text: Evidence: operating cash flow of 574 after interest paid on borrowings of 229, a working-capital outflow of 354 and taxes paid of 97; capital expenditure only 19; principal repayments 288; buybacks 96 (Q3 2026 report page:29, page:35). Risk mechanic: nine-month free cash flow of 555 funded the 288 repayments with surplus, but 185 of the working-capital outflow was other payables, including year-end accruals settled in 2026 (page:31), and interest paid (229) was below interest expense on borrowings (256) because 48 of interest was accrued but unpaid at September 30, 2026 (page:48). Credit implication: the next semi-annual coupon dates will pull more cash than the accrual-lagged nine-month figure suggests; debt service coverage should be tested on interest expense, not interest paid, when covenant definitions are available.

Credit implication: rate resets matter for the part of the floating-rate term loans not covered by swaps (term loans carry 2,600 at amortized cost against swap notional of 1,624; the bases differ, and the hedged allocation is not supplied), and the coupons on the secured and unsecured notes are not supplied.

facts.label: Business and transaction view
facts.text: Genmab A/S is a Danish, Nasdaq Copenhagen and Nasdaq-listed biotechnology company that earns most of its revenue from royalties on antibodies it created or enabled and sold by partners (J&J, Novartis, Amgen), and a growing share from its own co-commercialized products (EPKINLY/TEPKINLY with AbbVie, and Tivdak with Pfizer). In December 2025 it completed the cash acquisition of Merus, funded with a debt package that turned a net cash balance sheet into one with substantial secured and unsecured debt. The credit logic for a creditor is therefore a transfer of cash flow from a mature royalty stream, whose contractual horizon is disclosed and finite, to service debt incurred to buy a late-stage pipeline asset that does not yet produce revenue. Ownership is public and dispersed with no controlling holder, the issuer pays no dividends, and the debt documents restrict distributions, so sponsor-style extraction is not evident in the evidence supplied; the unrestricted capacity and covenant levels are not supplied, so that remains open. The binding source gaps are the executed debt documents and the audited annual report. This handoff is a context and transaction fact pack; it states no credit rating, no recovery outcome and no relative view.

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: On September 29, 2025 Genmab entered into a transaction agreement to acquire all shares of Merus N.V., which owned petosemtamab, for $97 per share in an all-cash transaction with a transaction value of approximately $8.0 billion, not subject to a financing condition, to be funded from cash on hand and approximately $5.5 billion of non-convertible debt backed by a funding commitment from Morgan Stanley Senior Funding, Inc. (Q3 2025 report page:3, page:40). The same report set a management target of gross leverage below 3x within two years after closing and said the package included a meaningful portion of prepayable debt (page:3); the leverage definition is not supplied. A wholly owned subsidiary commenced the tender offer on October 21, 2025 (page:3). The transaction closed on December 12, 2025, earlier than the early-2026 closing then expected (20-F page:125; Q3 2025 report page:40). It was accounted for as an asset acquisition because substantially all of the fair value was concentrated in petosemtamab (Q3 2026 report page:39); the auditor's critical audit matter cites an acquisition cost of USD 8.017 billion (20-F page:187).

facts.label: Transaction summary and new debt issues
facts.text: Financing: in December 2025 Genmab entered into a $1 billion Term Loan A Facility, a $2 billion Term Loan B Facility and a $500 million revolving credit facility, issued $1.5 billion principal amount of Senior Secured Notes and $1.0 billion principal amount of Senior Unsecured Notes (20-F page:126), and states it incurred borrowings of $5.5 billion and used cash on hand (Q3 2026 report page:6). The term loans and notes sum to $5.5 billion on the facility sizes, which is consistent with the revolver having been undrawn at closing; this is an Analyst Interpretation, because no supplied source states the revolver balance. The indenture is dated December 3, 2025 among Genmab A/S, Genmab Finance LLC, the guarantors named therein and Wilmington Trust, National Association as trustee and notes collateral agent, and a first supplemental indenture is dated January 28, 2026 (20-F page:180, page:181); their terms are not supplied. At September 30, 2026 borrowings carried at amortized cost were Term A Loans (secured), Term B Loans (secured), Secured Notes and Unsecured Notes of 4,992 in total (Q3 2026 report page:45; CP-1). Four interest rate swaps of 406 each convert part of the floating-rate debt to fixed rates between 3.3355% and 3.4885% against 3-month SOFR to 6/30/2028 (Q3 2026 report page:47). In June 2026 an amendment to the credit agreement reduced the Term B margin from 3.00% to 2.00%, with a modification gain of 23 (page:46); financial covenants are stated for the Term A Loans, with compliance stated at March 31, 2026 and September 30, 2026 and no levels given (Q1 2026 report page:35; Q3 2026 report page:46).

facts.label: Credit translations
facts.text: 1. Revenue durability (Evidence, Risk Mechanic, Credit Implication). Evidence: F6 and F7 and nine-month DARZALEX royalties of 2,057 out of revenue of 3,238 (CP-1). Risk mechanic: royalties are earned country by country until the later of a fixed term after first sale or the last Genmab patent expiry, which the filing places in 2029 to 2031 for the issued daratumumab patents, and are reduced where biosimilars launch or there is no patent coverage; J&J can terminate on 150 days' notice but then Genmab gains rights. Credit implication: debt service in later years must increasingly come from epcoritamab, Rina-S and petosemtamab, not from DARZALEX royalties. Whether that matters depends on debt maturities, which are not supplied (gap G1). Management Language on 2027 launches is not adopted. 2. Asset base and recovery mechanics (no recovery conclusion). Evidence: F1, F4 and CP-1 figures: goodwill and intangibles 9,197 including acquired IPR&D 8,237 against total assets 12,936. Risk mechanic: collateral value for the secured debt, as reflected on the balance sheet, is dominated by a pre-revenue pipeline asset acquired at a price set in 2025 rather than by cash-generating assets. Credit implication: if the pipeline asset underperforms, balance-sheet cover for creditors falls without any change in royalty cash flows; the security package is not supplied, so lien coverage is Not assessable. 3. Concentration and partner risk. Evidence: J&J accounts for 2,169 of revenue (Q3 2026 report page:39); AbbVie is the epcoritamab co-development partner, receives profit share of 184 on EPKINLY (page:23) and is the plaintiff in the Rina-S case (F14). Risk mechanic: relationship friction with a profit-sharing partner could affect co-commercialization decisions; litigation unquantified with no provision. Credit implication: contingent liability and partnership risk are unsized; this is an open item, not an adverse conclusion. 4. Sponsor alignment. Evidence: no sponsor, dispersed ownership, no dividends, buybacks continuing. Risk mechanic: equity holders are public investors rather than a financial sponsor, so distribution decisions are governed by the board and by the restricted payment covenants. Credit implication: leakage risk is low on documented actions but capacity for buybacks under the covenants is unknown (gap G4). 5. Counter-evidence logged: the Merus value appears as both "approximately $8.0 billion" and "USD 8.017 billion" (conflict C1). It does not weaken these translations.

rows.label: Genmab is a royalty-funded antibody developer that borrowed $5.5 billion to buy Merus, so creditors rely on DARZALEX and Kesimpta royalties while a pipeline asset matures. Ownership is dispersed and there are no dividends.
DARZALEX royalties are limited in time: Genmab's daratumumab patents expire in 2029 in the US, 2031 in Europe and 2030 in Japan, and J&J may terminate on 150 days' notice.
Merus was bought at $97 per share, about $8.0 billion, closed December 12, 2025, and financed with $5.5 billion of borrowings plus cash on hand.
Debt comprises Term A and Term B secured loans, $1.5 billion secured notes, $1.0 billion unsecured notes and a $500 million revolver.
No holder exceeds 5.80%, no dividends were paid in three years, yet buybacks continued, with $96 million spent in nine months 2026.
AbbVie, the epcoritamab co-development partner, is also the plaintiff in a trade secret case over Rina-S; no provision is recorded and no amount is stated.

facts.label: Credit view
facts.text: Genmab's fundamental credit is sound but now leveraged, and it can only be partly assessed. Its strongest support is a high-margin royalty stream: royalties were USD 2,699 million of USD 3,238 million revenue in the nine months to September 30, 2026, and operating cash flow of USD 574 million covered USD 288 million of principal repayments, taking net debt to USD 3,132 million. Its weakest point is that the largest royalty, DARZALEX, has a finite horizon, with Genmab's patents expiring between 2029 and 2031, while the new debt financed a pipeline asset that earns no revenue yet. The outcome will be decided by whether petosemtamab, Rina-S and epcoritamab launch in 2027 before royalties fade, tested against debt maturities and covenants that are not supplied.

facts.label: Key findings
facts.text: 1. Genmab moved from net cash to net debt and is paying it down. Borrowings at amortized cost were USD 4,992 million against cash of USD 1,860 million at September 30, 2026, so net debt was USD 3,132 million, down from USD 3,559 million at December 31, 2025, with USD 288 million of principal repaid in nine months 2026 [CP-1 Financials table; CP-1 Calculations]. Genmab had no borrowings before December 2025 [CP-1 Financial base view]. Category: Documentary Fact for the balances, Analyst Interpretation for the direction. 2. Leverage on EBITDA cannot be stated. FY2025 depreciation and amortization is only in the unsupplied audited statements, so LTM EBITDA is Not supplied [CP-1 Chart data: leverage]. EBIT-based references are 4.78x total debt and 3.00x net debt to LTM operating profit, which is a conservative upper reference because EBITDA exceeds operating profit. Management's stated aim of gross leverage below 3x within two years of closing cannot be tested without its definition [CP-1A F5]. Category: Insufficient Information for EBITDA leverage; Management Language for the target. 3. Interest cover is comfortable on the measure available. EBITDA of USD 1,068 million covered interest paid on borrowings of USD 229 million 4.66x over nine months 2026, and 3.54x in the first quarter; interest paid was below interest expense on borrowings of USD 256 million, consistent with USD 48 million of accrued interest on borrowings at September 30, 2026 [CP-1 Chart data: interest cover; CP-1 Evidence section]. Cover should be read as a strong-period figure, not a floor. Category: Analyst Interpretation (EBITDA is an analyst definition, not an issuer measure). 4. The cash stream behind the debt has a finite horizon. DARZALEX royalties were USD 2,057 million, 63.5% of nine-month revenue, J&J accounts for 67.0% of revenue, the royalty term runs to the later of 13 years after first sale or the last relevant patent expiry, the daratumumab patents expire in 2029 (US), 2031 (Europe) and 2030 (Japan), and J&J may terminate on 150 days' notice [CP-1 Financials table; CP-1A F6, F7]. Debt maturities are Not supplied, so overlap cannot be tested. Category: Documentary Fact. 5. Margins are compressing and guidance points lower for the fourth quarter. Operating margin was 30.4% against 37.8% a year earlier, adjusted operating expenses rose 27% while revenue rose 22%, and the guidance ranges imply fourth-quarter adjusted operating profit between negative USD 43 million and USD 277 million (midpoint USD 117 million) against USD 452 million in the third quarter [CP-1 Evidence section; CP-1 Calculations]. Category: Documentary Fact for the guidance; Analyst Interpretation for the implied quarter. Management attributes the spending to launch readiness; that is Management Language [CP-1A F15]. 6. Balance-sheet cover is concentrated in one asset. Goodwill and intangibles were USD 9,197 million, 71.1% of total assets, of which acquired IPR&D was USD 8,237 million; equity less goodwill and intangibles was negative USD 2,864 million [CP-1 Financials table]. The purchase was an asset acquisition concentrated in petosemtamab [CP-1A F4]. No recovery conclusion is drawn. Category: Documentary Fact. 7. Liquidity is visible only as cash. Cash was USD 1,860 million with no marketable securities, and current borrowings were USD 318 million; a USD 500 million revolver exists [CP-1A F16] but its availability is Not supplied [CP-1 Chart data: liquidity]. Category: Insufficient Information for committed liquidity. 8. Structure and covenants are only partly visible. The debt is secured Term A and Term B loans, secured notes of USD 1.5 billion and unsecured notes of USD 1.0 billion [CP-1A F3]; Term A Loans are subject to financial covenants with compliance stated and no levels [CP-1 Contingent claims section; CP-1A F10]. Guarantors, coupons and maturities are Not supplied. Category: Documentary Fact for what exists; Insufficient Information for terms.

facts.label: Strengths and weaknesses
facts.text: Strengths. (1) High-margin, partner-funded royalty income that covered debt service and principal repayments: royalties USD 2,699 million, operating cash flow USD 574 million, net debt reduction USD 427 million in nine months [CP-1 Financials table; Documentary Fact]. (2) Low capital intensity, with only USD 19 million of tangible and intangible investment in nine months 2026, so cash generation is not absorbed by capex [CP-1 Financials table; Documentary Fact]. (3) Royalties beyond DARZALEX: Kesimpta USD 408 million and TEPEZZA USD 93 million in nine months 2026, with Novartis and Amgen as licensees [CP-1A operating model; Documentary Fact]. (4) Interest-rate hedges: four swaps totalling USD 1,624 million of notional to June 30, 2028 and a Term B margin cut from 3.00% to 2.00% [CP-1 Evidence section; Documentary Fact]; the saving is an upper bound near USD 19 million a year because the Term B balance has since fallen [CP-1A Transaction section, correcting CP-1]. (5) Ownership and distributions: no controlling shareholder, no sponsor, no dividends in three years, and distributions restricted by the debt documents [CP-1A F8, F9, F13; Documentary Fact]. (6) Deleveraging in practice: USD 288 million of repayments in nine months 2026 and a stated leverage target [CP-1A F5; Management Language, not adopted].

(2) Finite royalty horizon from 2029 to 2031 for the issued patents, with a licensee termination right [CP-1A F6, F7; Documentary Fact]. (4) Rising cost base: adjusted operating expenses up 27% and operating margin down to 30.4%, with fourth-quarter guidance implying lower profit [CP-1 Evidence section; Analyst Interpretation]. (5) Floating-rate and refinancing exposure that cannot be sized: term loans of USD 2,600 million at amortized cost against USD 1,624 million of swap notional, on different bases, with maturities Not supplied [CP-1 Calculations; Insufficient Information]. (6) Unquantified contingent claims: AbbVie, a profit-sharing partner on epcoritamab, is the plaintiff in a trade secret case over Rina-S, with no provision recorded and no amount stated, and patent suits by Chugai in Japan [CP-1A F14; Documentary Fact; exposure is Insufficient Information].

spans.text: ## Request

Module: source readiness for GENMAB A/S (issuer id gmab), as of 2026-11-05 (cutoff 2026-11-05). Pathway: credit_snapshot. Reporting currency per the run context: USD; current period Q3 2026 (three and nine months ended September 30, 2026); prior period FY2025. Selected downstream consumers: CP-1, CP-1A, CP-2 and CP-5, for the report sections key findings, company operating model, model chart strip, financials and credit metrics, strengths and weaknesses, company profile and transaction summary.

Question answered: can the four supplied filings support that work, and what remains blocked. This handoff gives no credit conclusion, legal interpretation or investment opinion, and it normalizes, reconciles and calculates no financial figure. It is a source-sufficiency assessment only (SOURCE_SUFFICIENCY_ONLY; CP_MODEL_INPUT_CONTRACT_NOT_EVALUATED).

Perimeter: the reporting entity is the Genmab consolidated Group, that is Genmab A/S (parent, CVR 2102 3884) and its subsidiaries. The Q3 2026 report states: "The interim report is prepared on a consolidated basis for Genmab A/S (parent company) and its subsidiaries." (page:18). The run context names no borrower, parent, guarantor, sponsor or deal terms (all blank or empty); blank values are not treated as zero.
## Sources

## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| The four filings can support a credit snapshot of Genmab as of 2026-11-05, with limitations. Genmab now reports $4,992 million of borrowings against $1,860 million of cash, so debt terms matter, and those are largely missing. | Medium | The audited 2025 financial statements and the credit agreement and indenture terms are not in the pack, so maturities, coupons, covenant levels and revolver availability cannot be sourced. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Statements, notes and prior-year comparatives for the three and nine months to September 30, 2026 are present in full text. | Current-period flows, balance sheet and facility carrying values can be extracted, but the report is not audited or reviewed. | High |

| Full-year 2025 appears only as comparatives in interim reports; the audited statements are incorporated by reference but not supplied. | Full-year 2025 detail beyond key figures and the year-end balance sheet cannot be traced to audited statements. | High |

| Borrowings sit in four instruments with carrying values disclosed, but coupons, maturities and covenant levels are not. | Refinancing timing, interest burden by instrument and covenant headroom cannot be assessed from this pack. | High |

| No first-half 2026 report is supplied, and 2025 comparatives were reclassified in the latest report. | Discrete second-quarter 2026 figures and like-for-like expense lines need explicit bridging downstream. | Medium |
### Readiness view

The effective source set is READY_WITH_LIMITATIONS for the selected work. No selected consumer is CONDITIONAL or BLOCKED. Identity is unambiguous: all four documents are issued by Genmab A/S, in USD million, on a consolidated basis, and the run context currency (USD) matches the sources. The current-period evidence (Q3 2026 and nine months 2026, with Q3 2025 and nine months 2025 comparatives) is complete in extracted text, including income statement, balance sheet, cash flow, equity statement, a borrowings note with facility-level carrying values, derivative, lease, contingency and subsequent-event notes. The binding restrictions are: (a) the audited FY2025 financial statements and the annual-report notes on borrowings are not in the pack; (b) the executed credit agreement and indentures are listed as exhibits but not supplied; (c) no first-half 2026 report is supplied; (d) the 2026 interim statements are unaudited. These restrict, rather than prevent, each consumer, as set out in the consumer table below. This is a source-sufficiency judgment only; it does not accept any downstream input contract.
### Source assessments
#### 20-F for the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025

- Identity and authority: the cover page states "Form 20-F" for "the fiscal year ended December 31, 2025" by "Genmab A/S" (page:1). It is a filed annual report and controls its own narrative facts (business, risk factors, governance, exhibits list).

- What is present: business, risk factors including "Risks Related to Our Indebtedness" (page:64), Item 5 narrative (page:126 to page:132), exhibits list (page:180 to page:184), signature dated February 17, 2026 (page:185) and auditor reports (page:185 to page:190).

- What is not present: the financial statements themselves. Item 18 states "The financial statements required by this item are incorporated herein by reference to pages 107-156 of our Annual Report 2025" (page:180), and the Annual Report 2025 is Exhibit 15.3, listed as "Genmab A/S statutory Annual Report 2025*" (page:183). That exhibit is not part of the pack. Item 5 likewise incorporates by reference the Financial Review, liquidity, lease (Note 3.3), commitments (Note 5.3) and borrowings (Note 4.8) disclosures (page:130, page:131). Consequently no FY2025 income statement, balance sheet, cash flow statement or debt note is in this source's text.

- Debt facts that are present in narrative: December 2025 senior secured credit facilities of "a $1 billion Term Loan A Facility and a $2 billion Term Loan B Facility", "a $500 million revolving credit facility", "$1.5 billion principal amount of Senior Secured Notes and $1.0 billion principal amount of Senior Unsecured Notes" (page:126). The risk factor states the credit agreement "requires us to comply with certain financial maintenance covenants" (page:65), and the dividend discussion says the credit agreement and indentures restrict "restricted payments" (page:152).

- Currency: the 2023 auditor report records that the Company "changed the currency in which it presents its financial statements in 2025 from Danish Kroner to U.S. Dollar" (page:189), which is consistent with the USD context.
- Extraction: text extraction only; successful extraction is not a fidelity review, and no table image or XBRL tagging was inspected.
#### Interim report Q3 2025 (6-K Exhibit 99.1, November 6, 2025)
- Identity and period: nine months ended September 30, 2025 (page:1). Supplies the prior-year Q3 and nine-month base and the December 31, 2024 and full-year 2024 columns (page:4).

- Transaction evidence: the proposed Merus acquisition at "USD 97.00 per share in an all-cash transaction representing a transaction value of approximately USD 8.0 billion", expected funding "through a combination of cash on hand and approximately $5.5 billion of non-convertible debt financing", backed by a funding commitment from Morgan Stanley Senior Funding, Inc.; and a management target of "gross leverage <3x within two years after the closing" (page:3). This is a pre-closing statement and a management target, not an achieved outcome.

- Version relationship: this is the originally published presentation of the 2025 comparatives. The Q3 2026 report restates them (see the version log). The Q3 2025 report is retained as a separate active source and is not collapsed into the later one.
#### Interim report Q1 2026 (6-K Exhibit 99.1, May 7, 2026)
- Identity and period: three months ended March 31, 2026 (page:1), with full-year 2025 column in the key figures (page:3).

- Content: first-quarter statements, borrowings note by facility (page:35), covenant statement "Term Loan A is subject to financial covenants, with the financial covenant tests on a quarter-end basis beginning March 31, 2026" (page:35), swap schedule, legal and subsequent-event notes.
- Role: supplies discrete Q1 2026 and Q1 2025. Together with the nine-month report it brackets, but does not state, discrete Q2 2026.
#### Interim report Q3 2026 (6-K Exhibit 99.1, November 5, 2026)

- Identity and period: "Interim Report for the Nine Months Ended September 30, 2026" (page:1), dated on the run as-of date. Management states "The interim report has not been audited or reviewed by Genmab's external auditors" (page:37, page:54).

- Content: highlights and non-IFRS reconciliation (page:2, page:3), key figures (page:5, page:6), 2026 outlook table (page:6), financial review (page:18 to page:32), legal matters (page:33), statements (page:34 to page:36), notes 1 to 15 (page:37 to page:52).

- Debt: Note 8 gives current and non-current carrying values for Term A Loans (Secured), Term B Loans (Secured), Secured Notes and Unsecured Notes, a roll-forward from the December 31, 2025 balance, and the June 2026 amendment of the Term B margin "from 3.00% to 2.00%" with nominal value "$1,900 million" after the amendment (page:45, page:46). Note 9 gives four interest rate swaps with a fixed rate, 3-month SOFR index and termination date 6/30/2028 (page:47).

- Subsequent events: Note 15 states "No events have occurred subsequent to the balance sheet date that could significantly affect the condensed consolidated financial statements" (page:52). Separately, the highlights section lists October 2026 topline results of three Phase 3 trials (page:4). Both are dated on or before the cutoff and are treated as post-quarter events, not as period figures.

- Management claims, such as the CEO characterization of the data-rich fourth quarter and "first bispecific-based therapy approved in Europe for second-line FL" (page:1), are attributed management language, not filing-controlled facts.
- Extraction: text extraction only; no chart, image or speaker-note coverage is claimed (none applies; the documents are text exhibits).

### Report-model input sufficiency (source level only)

- Discrete quarters: Q3 2026 and Q3 2025 (Q3 2026 report, page:5); Q1 2026 and Q1 2025 (Q1 report, page:3). Discrete Q2 2026 is not stated in any supplied source because the first-half 2026 report is not supplied (the Q3 2026 report refers to it, page:8).
- Fiscal years: FY2025 and FY2024 key figures (Q3 2026 report page:5; Q3 2025 report page:4). The 20-F audit reports cover the years but the statements are not in the pack.
- Quarter versus year-to-date: the Q3 2026 report prints three-month and nine-month columns side by side (page:5, page:34). The cash flow statement prints nine months only (page:35).
- Segments: the report states Genmab is "managed and operated as one business unit" (page:39). Revenue by type, partner and royalty product is in Note 3 (page:39).
- Add-backs: the non-IFRS reconciliation for nine months 2026 and 2025 is on page:3. No quarter-level reconciliation table is supplied.
- Debt: facility-level carrying values and a roll-forward (page:45); cash interest "Interest paid on borrowings" and "Corporate taxes paid" are printed for nine months (page:35).

### Financial base view

The consolidated Group moved from no borrowings (September 30, 2025) to $4,992 million of borrowings after the December 2025 Merus financing, so the reported base now has two regimes: a pre-acquisition year with net cash and a post-acquisition year with net debt. Debt is carried at amortized cost in four instruments (Term A Loans, Term B Loans, Secured Notes, Unsecured Notes), all disclosed with current and non-current carrying values, and the Group had $1,860 million of cash and no marketable securities at September 30, 2026. On a carrying-value basis net debt was $3,132 million, down from $3,559 million at December 31, 2025, with principal repayments of $288 million in nine months 2026. The income base is royalty-led (royalties $2,699 million of $3,238 million revenue) and operating profit is $986 million for the nine months, with adjusted operating profit of $1,108 million on the company's own non-IFRS definition. The issuer reports no EBITDA, and the depreciation and amortization needed for a last-twelve-months EBITDA is not supplied for FY2025, so the leverage chart cannot be populated; EBIT-based reference ratios are given instead and are labelled as such. Interest cover is calculable for Q1 2026 and nine months 2026 only. Undrawn committed facilities, covenant levels and contractual maturities are Not supplied. The base is therefore sufficient for reported-fact extraction, cash and net debt, cash conversion and interest cover on a nine-month basis, and restricted for LTM leverage, liquidity headroom, maturity profile and covenant analysis.

### Evidence, risk mechanic and credit implication
#### Acquisition leverage rests on one intangible asset

Evidence: borrowings of 4,992 against shareholders' equity of 6,333, and goodwill and intangibles of 9,197 including acquired IPR&D of 8,237, which is 63.7% of total assets of 12,936 (Q3 2026 report page:5, page:34, page:40). Risk mechanic: the Merus purchase was accounted for as an asset acquisition concentrated in a single identifiable asset, petosemtamab (Q3 2026 report page:39), so the balance-sheet value that backs the debt depends on one pipeline asset that is not yet generating revenue; an adverse trial or regulatory outcome would impair the IPR&D and equity but would not by itself change cash debt service. Credit implication: asset-based recovery cover is weak relative to debt, and creditor protection rests on royalty cash flows and the covenants, not on the asset base. October 2026 topline results for petosemtamab were reported as meeting both primary endpoints (Q3 2026 report page:4); that is a post-quarter event and a management announcement, with no financial effect quantified in the supplied sources.
#### Margin compression reflects launch investment and is guided to continue

Evidence: adjusted operating expenses of 1,896 versus 1,489 (up 27%) against revenue up 22%, giving operating margin of 30.4% versus 37.8% (Q3 2026 report page:2, page:5). The full-year guidance of adjusted operating profit of 1,065 to 1,385 and revenue of 4,325 to 4,525 implies a fourth quarter below the third: adjusted operating profit of minus 43 to 277 (midpoint 117) versus 452 in Q3 2026, because 9M adjusted operating profit is 1,108. Risk mechanic: spending ahead of launches in 2027 is front-loaded while royalty growth is tied to partners' sales. Credit implication: EBITDA available for interest is not going to grow in line with revenue in the near term; the interest cover ratios above should be read as strong-quarter outcomes, not as a floor. Management language: guidance assumes no significant new agreements (page:6).
#### Cash flow covers debt service, but quality is mixed

Evidence: operating cash flow of 574 after interest paid on borrowings of 229, a working-capital outflow of 354 and taxes paid of 97; capital expenditure only 19; principal repayments 288; buybacks 96 (Q3 2026 report page:29, page:35). Risk mechanic: nine-month free cash flow of 555 funded the 288 repayments with surplus, but 185 of the working-capital outflow was other payables, including year-end accruals settled in 2026 (page:31), and interest paid (229) was below interest expense on borrowings (256) because 48 of interest was accrued but unpaid at September 30, 2026 (page:48). Credit implication: the next semi-annual coupon dates will pull more cash than the accrual-lagged nine-month figure suggests; debt service coverage should be tested on interest expense, not interest paid, when covenant definitions are available.
#### Revenue concentration and partner dependence

Evidence: DARZALEX royalties 2,057 are 63.5% of revenue, and J&J accounts for 2,169 or 67.0% of revenue (Q3 2026 report page:39, page:40). Risk mechanic: royalties are set by J&J's net sales and are reduced by the Halozyme royalty share and by territories without Genmab patent coverage (page:19, page:20); the DARZALEX royalty rose 18% versus J&J net sales up 19% (page:19). Credit implication: repayment capacity depends on one partner's product, with limited issuer control over sales, pricing or patent life; patent expiry terms are outside this handoff.
#### Interest-rate exposure and hedges

Evidence: floating-rate term loans indexed to 3-month SOFR, four swaps of 406 each (1,624 in total) at fixed rates between 3.3355% and 3.4885% to 6/30/2028, and a Term B margin cut from 3.00% to 2.00% in June 2026 on a nominal 1,900 (Q3 2026 report page:46, page:47). Risk mechanic: the swaps hedge part of the floating exposure for approximately two years (Q3 2026 report page:39); the margin cut lowers the contractual spread cost by about 19 a year on the nominal (1,900 x 1.00%), before any floor or step features that are not supplied. Credit implication: rate resets matter for the part of the floating-rate term loans not covered by swaps (term loans carry 2,600 at amortized cost against swap notional of 1,624; the bases differ, and the hedged allocation is not supplied), and the coupons on the secured and unsecured notes are not supplied.
#### Contingent claims and covenants

Evidence: patent and trade-secret litigation (Chugai in Japan; AbbVie in the U.S. District Court for the Western District of Washington) with no provisions recorded and no amounts stated (Q3 2026 report page:33, page:51); Term A Loans subject to financial covenants with compliance stated and no levels (page:46). Credit implication: contingent liabilities cannot be sized and covenant headroom cannot be calculated; both are open items, not zero.
### Definition review

- EBITDA: not reported by the issuer; the company reports adjusted operating profit excluding acquisition and integration charges and amortization of acquired intangibles (Q3 2026 report page:2, page:3). The analyst EBITDA above adds back depreciation (including right-of-use depreciation, so it is before lease depreciation but lease interest 5 is separately in financing costs) and amortization from the cash flow statement; it does not add back share-based compensation 124, impairment 27 or acquisition and integration charges 87. A variant adding back the latter two (87 + 27 = 114) gives 1,182 and cover of 5.16x on 229.

- Total debt: borrowings at amortized cost from the balance sheet, net of unamortized fees; nominal amounts are only partly supplied (Term B nominal 1,900; Notes principal as issued). Lease liabilities (206) are shown separately.
- Cash interest: "Interest paid on borrowings" in operating activities; other interest paid (2) and lease interest (5) are shown separately.
- Covenant EBITDA and total net leverage definitions are in the unsupplied credit agreement; the analyst EBITDA is not a covenant measure.
### Subsequent events and period labelling

Note 15 of the Q3 2026 report states no events subsequent to the balance sheet date that could significantly affect the statements (page:52). The three October 2026 Phase 3 topline results (epcoritamab EPCORE DLBCL-2, Rina-S RAINFOL-02, petosemtamab LiGeR-HN1) are listed in the report highlights (page:4) and are kept out of every period figure above. Periods used: Q3 2026 (three months), nine months 2026, Q1 2026, LTM September 30, 2026, FY2025 and balance sheet dates of September 30, 2026, March 31, 2026, December 31, 2025 and September 30, 2025. No nine-month amount is presented as a full-year amount.

### Business and transaction view

Genmab A/S is a Danish, Nasdaq Copenhagen and Nasdaq-listed biotechnology company that earns most of its revenue from royalties on antibodies it created or enabled and sold by partners (J&J, Novartis, Amgen), and a growing share from its own co-commercialized products (EPKINLY/TEPKINLY with AbbVie, and Tivdak with Pfizer). In December 2025 it completed the cash acquisition of Merus, funded with a debt package that turned a net cash balance sheet into one with substantial secured and unsecured debt. The credit logic for a creditor is therefore a transfer of cash flow from a mature royalty stream, whose contractual horizon is disclosed and finite, to service debt incurred to buy a late-stage pipeline asset that does not yet produce revenue. Ownership is public and dispersed with no controlling holder, the issuer pays no dividends, and the debt documents restrict distributions, so sponsor-style extraction is not evident in the evidence supplied; the unrestricted capacity and covenant levels are not supplied, so that remains open. The binding source gaps are the executed debt documents and the audited annual report. This handoff is a context and transaction fact pack; it states no credit rating, no recovery outcome and no relative view.

### Transaction summary and new debt issues

On September 29, 2025 Genmab entered into a transaction agreement to acquire all shares of Merus N.V., which owned petosemtamab, for $97 per share in an all-cash transaction with a transaction value of approximately $8.0 billion, not subject to a financing condition, to be funded from cash on hand and approximately $5.5 billion of non-convertible debt backed by a funding commitment from Morgan Stanley Senior Funding, Inc. (Q3 2025 report page:3, page:40). The same report set a management target of gross leverage below 3x within two years after closing and said the package included a meaningful portion of prepayable debt (page:3); the leverage definition is not supplied. A wholly owned subsidiary commenced the tender offer on October 21, 2025 (page:3). The transaction closed on December 12, 2025, earlier than the early-2026 closing then expected (20-F page:125; Q3 2025 report page:40). It was accounted for as an asset acquisition because substantially all of the fair value was concentrated in petosemtamab (Q3 2026 report page:39); the auditor's critical audit matter cites an acquisition cost of USD 8.017 billion (20-F page:187).

Financing: in December 2025 Genmab entered into a $1 billion Term Loan A Facility, a $2 billion Term Loan B Facility and a $500 million revolving credit facility, issued $1.5 billion principal amount of Senior Secured Notes and $1.0 billion principal amount of Senior Unsecured Notes (20-F page:126), and states it incurred borrowings of $5.5 billion and used cash on hand (Q3 2026 report page:6). The term loans and notes sum to $5.5 billion on the facility sizes, which is consistent with the revolver having been undrawn at closing; this is an Analyst Interpretation, because no supplied source states the revolver balance. The indenture is dated December 3, 2025 among Genmab A/S, Genmab Finance LLC, the guarantors named therein and Wilmington Trust, National Association as trustee and notes collateral agent, and a first supplemental indenture is dated January 28, 2026 (20-F page:180, page:181); their terms are not supplied. At September 30, 2026 borrowings carried at amortized cost were Term A Loans (secured), Term B Loans (secured), Secured Notes and Unsecured Notes of 4,992 in total (Q3 2026 report page:45; CP-1). Four interest rate swaps of 406 each convert part of the floating-rate debt to fixed rates between 3.3355% and 3.4885% against 3-month SOFR to 6/30/2028 (Q3 2026 report page:47). In June 2026 an amendment to the credit agreement reduced the Term B margin from 3.00% to 2.00%, with a modification gain of 23 (page:46); financial covenants are stated for the Term A Loans, with compliance stated at March 31, 2026 and September 30, 2026 and no levels given (Q1 2026 report page:35; Q3 2026 report page:46).

Status and subsequent events: all of the above were executed before the cutoff. After the quarter, October 2026 topline results were reported for three Phase 3 trials (Q3 2026 report page:4); Note 15 reports no events that could significantly affect the statements (page:52). No new debt issue after September 30, 2026 appears in the pack. Correction to the financial handoff: it estimated a Term B margin saving of about 19 a year on a nominal of 1,900, which is the nominal immediately after the June 2026 amendment (Q3 2026 report page:46); because 250 of Term B principal was repaid in nine months 2026 (page:45), the nominal outstanding at September 30, 2026 is not printed and is lower, so the saving is lower than that estimate. The 19 figure should be read as an upper bound at the amendment date.

| F16 | Revolver existence | Documentary Fact | High | 20-F page:126 | a $500 million revolving credit facility |
### Governance and sponsor behaviour (issuer level)

Assessment: Neutral or Mixed, with Insufficient Information on distribution capacity. Evidence from documented actions only: no controlling shareholder and no sponsor (F13, run context); no dividends in three years (F8); no material related-party transactions (Q3 2026 report page:49); principal repayments of 288 in nine months 2026 (CP-1; Q3 2026 report page:35), which is Supportive of deleveraging; against that, continued share buybacks of 96 in nine months 2026 (F12; Q3 2026 report page:44) and two large acquisitions since 2024 (ProfoundBio in the second quarter of 2024 per Q3 2026 report page:41, and Merus), which does not by itself establish an appetite for further acquisitions. No creditor-adverse transaction such as priming, uptiering, drop-down or non-pro-rata exchange appears in the pack. Not supplied: restricted payment baskets, debt incurrence capacity and covenant certificates, which are in the executed documents. Evidence quality: High for the actions listed; Insufficient for covenant capacity. Evidence limits: this reads issuer behaviour only; it makes no statement about any individual.
### Credit translations

1. Revenue durability (Evidence, Risk Mechanic, Credit Implication). Evidence: F6 and F7 and nine-month DARZALEX royalties of 2,057 out of revenue of 3,238 (CP-1). Risk mechanic: royalties are earned country by country until the later of a fixed term after first sale or the last Genmab patent expiry, which the filing places in 2029 to 2031 for the issued daratumumab patents, and are reduced where biosimilars launch or there is no patent coverage; J&J can terminate on 150 days' notice but then Genmab gains rights. Credit implication: debt service in later years must increasingly come from epcoritamab, Rina-S and petosemtamab, not from DARZALEX royalties. Whether that matters depends on debt maturities, which are not supplied (gap G1). Management Language on 2027 launches is not adopted.

2. Asset base and recovery mechanics (no recovery conclusion). Evidence: F1, F4 and CP-1 figures: goodwill and intangibles 9,197 including acquired IPR&D 8,237 against total assets 12,936. Risk mechanic: collateral value for the secured debt, as reflected on the balance sheet, is dominated by a pre-revenue pipeline asset acquired at a price set in 2025 rather than by cash-generating assets. Credit implication: if the pipeline asset underperforms, balance-sheet cover for creditors falls without any change in royalty cash flows; the security package is not supplied, so lien coverage is Not assessable.

3. Concentration and partner risk. Evidence: J&J accounts for 2,169 of revenue (Q3 2026 report page:39); AbbVie is the epcoritamab co-development partner, receives profit share of 184 on EPKINLY (page:23) and is the plaintiff in the Rina-S case (F14). Risk mechanic: relationship friction with a profit-sharing partner could affect co-commercialization decisions; litigation unquantified with no provision. Credit implication: contingent liability and partnership risk are unsized; this is an open item, not an adverse conclusion.

4. Sponsor alignment. Evidence: no sponsor, dispersed ownership, no dividends, buybacks continuing. Risk mechanic: equity holders are public investors rather than a financial sponsor, so distribution decisions are governed by the board and by the restricted payment covenants. Credit implication: leakage risk is low on documented actions but capacity for buybacks under the covenants is unknown (gap G4).
5. Counter-evidence logged: the Merus value appears as both "approximately $8.0 billion" and "USD 8.017 billion" (conflict C1). It does not weaken these translations.

Fundamental credit synthesis for GENMAB A/S (issuer id gmab) as of 2026-11-05, pathway credit_snapshot, in USD millions, built only from the accepted financial and business handoffs. It covers business risk, financial risk, liquidity and the gaps that limit them, and gives no peer ranking, instrument recommendation or recovery conclusion.
## Sources

| CP-1 | 470d2d1ddbdc4449f689b20b3d5a9b49f6d69c93c24a1bf1e1eda3c8703c07f5 | Financial base and metrics, cited as [CP-1 Financials table] and [CP-1 Calculations] |
| CP-1A | 97ef47d35b1d1d1c1be5913dc3a9164537ae157cdc8b548f9cf30fdc89277154 | Business and transaction facts F1 to F16, cited as [CP-1A F1] and so on, and its conflicts and gaps G1 to G10 |
## Findings
### Reader summary
| Bottom line | Confidence | Main limitation |

| Genmab's royalty income is strong and net debt is falling, but it borrowed to buy a pipeline asset and its largest royalty has a finite horizon, so the credit is sound but leveraged and only partly assessable. | Medium | Debt maturities, coupons, covenant levels, revolver availability, ratings and full-year 2025 depreciation are not supplied, so leverage on EBITDA, liquidity headroom and refinancing timing cannot be tested. |
| Finding | Creditor impact | Confidence |

| Net debt fell from USD 3,559 million to USD 3,132 million in nine months while USD 288 million of principal was repaid. | Deleveraging is real and funded from operations, which supports repayment capacity. | Medium |

| EBITDA covered cash interest 4.66x over nine months 2026, and interest paid was USD 229 million. | Cover is comfortable on this measure, but the coupon schedule and floating-rate resets are not fully disclosed. | Medium |

| DARZALEX royalties were 63.5% of revenue, and Genmab's daratumumab patents expire in 2029, 2030 and 2031. | The main debt-servicing cash stream has a finite horizon that debt maturities, once known, must be tested against. | High |

| Goodwill and intangibles of USD 9,197 million are 71.1% of total assets, mostly the acquired petosemtamab asset. | Balance-sheet cover for creditors depends on one pre-revenue asset, so cash flow, not assets, carries repayment. | High |
| Guidance implies fourth-quarter 2026 adjusted operating profit well below the third quarter. | Nine-month coverage should not be extrapolated; launch spending is front-loaded. | Medium |
### Credit view

Genmab's fundamental credit is sound but now leveraged, and it can only be partly assessed. Its strongest support is a high-margin royalty stream: royalties were USD 2,699 million of USD 3,238 million revenue in the nine months to September 30, 2026, and operating cash flow of USD 574 million covered USD 288 million of principal repayments, taking net debt to USD 3,132 million. Its weakest point is that the largest royalty, DARZALEX, has a finite horizon, with Genmab's patents expiring between 2029 and 2031, while the new debt financed a pipeline asset that earns no revenue yet. The outcome will be decided by whether petosemtamab, Rina-S and epcoritamab launch in 2027 before royalties fade, tested against debt maturities and covenants that are not supplied.
### Credit assessment
| Assessment | Category | Confidence | Basis | Limitation |

| Sound but leveraged: royalty cash flow supports debt service and deleveraging, with material single-product concentration and an asset base dominated by one acquired pipeline asset | Analyst Interpretation | Medium | [CP-1 Financials table: net debt, cash flow, interest cover]; [CP-1A F1, F2, F6, F7] | Confidence is held at Medium, below High, because debt maturities, coupons, covenant levels, revolver availability and ratings are Not supplied [CP-1A G1, G2, G3, G4] |

| Thesis: a mature royalty stream is servicing and repaying debt taken on to buy a late-stage asset, and creditworthiness depends on that asset's 2027 launches arriving before the DARZALEX royalty horizon closes | Analyst Interpretation | Medium | [CP-1A F1, F2, F6]; [CP-1 Financials table: DARZALEX share of revenue] | The royalty horizon cannot be compared with debt maturities until the debt documents are added |
### Key findings

1. Genmab moved from net cash to net debt and is paying it down. Borrowings at amortized cost were USD 4,992 million against cash of USD 1,860 million at September 30, 2026, so net debt was USD 3,132 million, down from USD 3,559 million at December 31, 2025, with USD 288 million of principal repaid in nine months 2026 [CP-1 Financials table; CP-1 Calculations]. Genmab had no borrowings before December 2025 [CP-1 Financial base view]. Category: Documentary Fact for the balances, Analyst Interpretation for the direction.

2. Leverage on EBITDA cannot be stated. FY2025 depreciation and amortization is only in the unsupplied audited statements, so LTM EBITDA is Not supplied [CP-1 Chart data: leverage]. EBIT-based references are 4.78x total debt and 3.00x net debt to LTM operating profit, which is a conservative upper reference because EBITDA exceeds operating profit. Management's stated aim of gross leverage below 3x within two years of closing cannot be tested without its definition [CP-1A F5]. Category: Insufficient Information for EBITDA leverage; Management Language for the target.

3. Interest cover is comfortable on the measure available. EBITDA of USD 1,068 million covered interest paid on borrowings of USD 229 million 4.66x over nine months 2026, and 3.54x in the first quarter; interest paid was below interest expense on borrowings of USD 256 million, consistent with USD 48 million of accrued interest on borrowings at September 30, 2026 [CP-1 Chart data: interest cover; CP-1 Evidence section]. Cover should be read as a strong-period figure, not a floor. Category: Analyst Interpretation (EBITDA is an analyst definition, not an issuer measure).

4. The cash stream behind the debt has a finite horizon. DARZALEX royalties were USD 2,057 million, 63.5% of nine-month revenue, J&J accounts for 67.0% of revenue, the royalty term runs to the later of 13 years after first sale or the last relevant patent expiry, the daratumumab patents expire in 2029 (US), 2031 (Europe) and 2030 (Japan), and J&J may terminate on 150 days' notice [CP-1 Financials table; CP-1A F6, F7]. Debt maturities are Not supplied, so overlap cannot be tested. Category: Documentary Fact.

5. Margins are compressing and guidance points lower for the fourth quarter. Operating margin was 30.4% against 37.8% a year earlier, adjusted operating expenses rose 27% while revenue rose 22%, and the guidance ranges imply fourth-quarter adjusted operating profit between negative USD 43 million and USD 277 million (midpoint USD 117 million) against USD 452 million in the third quarter [CP-1 Evidence section; CP-1 Calculations]. Category: Documentary Fact for the guidance; Analyst Interpretation for the implied quarter. Management attributes the spending to launch readiness; that is Management Language [CP-1A F15].

6. Balance-sheet cover is concentrated in one asset. Goodwill and intangibles were USD 9,197 million, 71.1% of total assets, of which acquired IPR&D was USD 8,237 million; equity less goodwill and intangibles was negative USD 2,864 million [CP-1 Financials table]. The purchase was an asset acquisition concentrated in petosemtamab [CP-1A F4]. No recovery conclusion is drawn. Category: Documentary Fact.

7. Liquidity is visible only as cash. Cash was USD 1,860 million with no marketable securities, and current borrowings were USD 318 million; a USD 500 million revolver exists [CP-1A F16] but its availability is Not supplied [CP-1 Chart data: liquidity]. Category: Insufficient Information for committed liquidity.

8. Structure and covenants are only partly visible. The debt is secured Term A and Term B loans, secured notes of USD 1.5 billion and unsecured notes of USD 1.0 billion [CP-1A F3]; Term A Loans are subject to financial covenants with compliance stated and no levels [CP-1 Contingent claims section; CP-1A F10]. Guarantors, coupons and maturities are Not supplied. Category: Documentary Fact for what exists; Insufficient Information for terms.
### Strengths and weaknesses

Strengths. (1) High-margin, partner-funded royalty income that covered debt service and principal repayments: royalties USD 2,699 million, operating cash flow USD 574 million, net debt reduction USD 427 million in nine months [CP-1 Financials table; Documentary Fact]. (2) Low capital intensity, with only USD 19 million of tangible and intangible investment in nine months 2026, so cash generation is not absorbed by capex [CP-1 Financials table; Documentary Fact]. (3) Royalties beyond DARZALEX: Kesimpta USD 408 million and TEPEZZA USD 93 million in nine months 2026, with Novartis and Amgen as licensees [CP-1A operating model; Documentary Fact]. (4) Interest-rate hedges: four swaps totalling USD 1,624 million of notional to June 30, 2028 and a Term B margin cut from 3.00% to 2.00% [CP-1 Evidence section; Documentary Fact]; the saving is an upper bound near USD 19 million a year because the Term B balance has since fallen [CP-1A Transaction section, correcting CP-1]. (5) Ownership and distributions: no controlling shareholder, no sponsor, no dividends in three years, and distributions restricted by the debt documents [CP-1A F8, F9, F13; Documentary Fact]. (6) Deleveraging in practice: USD 288 million of repayments in nine months 2026 and a stated leverage target [CP-1A F5; Management Language, not adopted].

Weaknesses. (1) Concentration: DARZALEX royalties are 63.5% of revenue and J&J 67.0% [CP-1 Financials table; Documentary Fact]. (2) Finite royalty horizon from 2029 to 2031 for the issued patents, with a licensee termination right [CP-1A F6, F7; Documentary Fact]. (3) Leverage built for an acquisition: borrowings of USD 4,992 million against equity of USD 6,333 million, with the asset base dominated by an unproven pipeline asset [CP-1 Financials table; CP-1A F1, F2, F4; Documentary Fact]. (4) Rising cost base: adjusted operating expenses up 27% and operating margin down to 30.4%, with fourth-quarter guidance implying lower profit [CP-1 Evidence section; Analyst Interpretation]. (5) Floating-rate and refinancing exposure that cannot be sized: term loans of USD 2,600 million at amortized cost against USD 1,624 million of swap notional, on different bases, with maturities Not supplied [CP-1 Calculations; Insufficient Information]. (6) Unquantified contingent claims: AbbVie, a profit-sharing partner on epcoritamab, is the plaintiff in a trade secret case over Rina-S, with no provision recorded and no amount stated, and patent suits by Chugai in Japan [CP-1A F14; Documentary Fact; exposure is Insufficient Information].
### Key credit risks
| Risk | Mechanic | Credit implication | Severity | Basis |

| Royalty horizon closes before the pipeline replaces it | Largest royalty is time-limited by patents expiring 2029 to 2031 and is terminable on 150 days' notice; debt service later relies on epcoritamab, Rina-S and petosemtamab | Debt service capacity after the royalty horizon depends on 2027 launches; overlap with debt maturities is untested | Material | [CP-1A F6, F7]; [CP-1 DARZALEX share] |

| Single-asset balance-sheet cover | Acquired IPR&D of USD 8,237 million is 63.7% of total assets; an adverse trial or regulatory result impairs equity without changing cash debt service | Asset-based cover for secured creditors weakens; security package not supplied | Material | [CP-1A F4]; [CP-1 Financials table] |

| Refinancing and maturity profile unknown | Contractual maturities, amortization and call terms are not supplied; current borrowings USD 318 million | Cannot test refinancing wall against cash flow | Material | [CP-1A G1]; [CP-1 Chart data: debt maturities] |

| Covenant headroom unknown | Term A Loans have maintenance covenants tested quarterly since March 31, 2026; compliance stated, levels not | A margin decline could pressure headroom with no way to size it | Material | [CP-1A F10, G4] |
| Margin compression | Adjusted operating expenses rising faster than revenue ahead of 2027 launches | Interest cover and free cash flow fall if royalties slow | Material | [CP-1 Evidence section] |

| Partner litigation and contingent claims | AbbVie case and Chugai suits unquantified, no provisions | Possible cash cost and partner friction; exposure Not supplied | Minor, pending quantification | [CP-1A F14, G6] |
| Floating-rate cost | Term loans floating on 3-month SOFR; swaps to June 30, 2028 cover part | Rate rises raise interest paid on the unhedged part | Minor | [CP-1 Evidence section] |
## Calculations
New calculations in this module, from CP-1 figures only:
| Calculation | Inputs | Result |
| Cash as a share of borrowings, September 30, 2026 | 1,860 / 4,992 | 37.3% |
| Borrowings to shareholders' equity, September 30, 2026 | 4,992 / 6,333 | 0.79x |

All other figures are restated from CP-1 without change (borrowings USD 4,992 million; net debt USD 3,132 million; nine-month interest cover 4.66x; DARZALEX share 63.5%; operating margin 30.4%). Consistency checks against upstream: CP-1 and CP-1A agree on the DARZALEX royalty (USD 2,057 million), J&J revenue (USD 2,169 million), net debt and the swap notional (USD 1,624 million). Correction carried: CP-1 estimated the Term B margin saving at about USD 19 million a year on a nominal of USD 1,900 million; CP-1A showed that nominal is the figure immediately after the June 2026 amendment and the current balance is lower, so this module treats USD 19 million as an upper bound.
## Gaps
| Gap | Severity | What it affects | Action |

| Debt maturity schedule, coupons, call terms, security and guarantors Not supplied [CP-1A G1] | High | Refinancing risk, royalty-horizon overlap, security coverage | Add the credit agreement, indentures and Note 4.8 |
| Revolver balance and availability Not supplied [CP-1A G2] | High | Liquidity headroom | Add Note 4.8 |
| Covenant levels, definitions and restricted-payment capacity Not supplied [CP-1A G4] | High | Headroom and buyback capacity | Add executed documents |
| LTM EBITDA and FY2025 depreciation and amortization Not supplied [CP-1 Gaps] | High | EBITDA leverage and the leverage target | Add Annual Report 2025 |
| Credit ratings Not supplied [CP-1A G3] | Medium | External cross-check | Add rating reports; label as external |
| Leverage target definition Not supplied [CP-1A G5] | Medium | Testing management's target | Add management definition |
| Litigation and commitments unquantified [CP-1A G6, G7] | Medium | Contingent cash calls | Add Notes 5.3 and 5.7 of the annual report |
| Discrete Q2 2026 and Q3 2026 cash interest not supplied | Medium | Quarterly cover | Add first-half 2026 report |
